profile.summary: LlaSMol-Mistral-7B is a chemistry language model: Mistral-7B-v0.1 with a LoRA adapter trained on SMolInstruct, a dataset of 14 small molecule tasks and more than three million instruction samples. It answers questions about molecules in text, with chemical content marked by tags such as SMILES and IUPAC, covering name conversion, property prediction, molecule captioning and generation, and reaction prediction. It is in this database because the DeepProtein benchmark prompted it for protein properties without fine-tuning it; its own developers describe no protein task.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: LlaSMol-Mistral-7B is Mistral-7B-v0.1 with a LoRA adapter trained on SMolInstruct, an instruction tuning dataset of 14 chemistry tasks and more than three million samples. The released repository holds the adapter only, about 84 MB, not a full set of weights: the adapter config gives rank 16, alpha 16, dropout 0.05 and the seven projection modules it adapts. Queries and answers use tags that mark the type of each piece of content, for example SMILES, IUPAC, MOLFORMULA, NUMBER and BOOLEAN, and the repository code canonicalises any SMILES wrapped in its tags.

quotes.text: It is based on [mistralai/Mistral-7B-v0.1](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-7B-v0.1) and tuned on our [SMolInstruct](https://huggingface.co/datasets/osunlp/SMolInstruct) dataset with LoRA. This repo contains the weight of the low-rank adapter.
It contains 14 selected chemistry tasks and over three million samples
The code would canonicalize SMILES string automatically, as long as it is wrapped in `<SMILES> ... </SMILES>`.

sections.title: What it is built for
sections.body: The README groups the trained tasks into four types: name conversion between IUPAC names, SMILES and molecular formulae; property prediction on the ESOL, LIPO, BBBP, ClinTox, HIV and SIDER datasets; molecule captioning and generation from a description; and chemical reaction tasks, forward synthesis and retrosynthesis. All of these are small molecule tasks. Protein sequences are not among them. The record exists because the DeepProtein benchmark prompted the model for protein properties, wrapping the sequence in PROTEIN tags, without fine-tuning it.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Four LlaSMol models are released, one per base model: LlaSMol-Galactica-6.7B, LlaSMol-Llama2-7B, LlaSMol-CodeLlama-7B and LlaSMol-Mistral-7B. The paper reports Mistral as the best base model for chemistry tasks. Each repository holds a LoRA adapter, so a run must name both the adapter revision and the base model it was applied to; this page read osunlp/LlaSMol-Mistral-7B at revision 044d6124 over mistralai/Mistral-7B-v0.1. The code is at github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/LLM4Chem, read here at commit 43ab5fcc, and includes the three step evaluation scripts for SMolInstruct.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Mistral-7B-v0.1 decoder with a LoRA adapter: rank 16, alpha 16, dropout 0.05, applied to q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, o_proj, gate_proj, up_proj and down_proj, task type causal language modelling.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: A natural language query with typed tags around chemical content: SMILES in <SMILES> tags and IUPAC names in <IUPAC> tags. In the protein benchmark the sequence was wrapped in PROTEIN tags instead.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Generated text with the answer inside a tag: MOLFORMULA, SMILES, IUPAC, NUMBER or BOOLEAN. The repository's extraction script takes the part between those tags and treats a missing tag as no answer.

quotes.text: If the tags are missing or incomplete, the extracted answer will be empty and regarded as "no answer" in metric calculation.

strengths.text: The released file is a LoRA adapter of about 84 MB, so it is cheap to download and to store next to a base model.

strengths.text: The repository ships a short generation interface plus the three step pipeline the authors used to evaluate on their own dataset, so results can be reproduced with the published scripts.
The tag format gives a machine readable answer, and the repository's own extraction script pulls it out of the generated text.
The adapter weights are under CC BY 4.0, and the training dataset SMolInstruct is published on Hugging Face.

run_guide.summary: Clone the official repository and query the released adapter with the two line generation example from its README.
prerequisites: The code repository, which the README says to clone before running anything.
Access to the base model mistralai/Mistral-7B-v0.1 under its own terms, since the released repository holds only the LoRA adapter.
A GPU able to hold a 7B parameter model; the README's fine-tuning example uses four GPUs, and the sources state no inference requirement.
Chemical content in the query must be wrapped in the tags the README lists.

steps.title: Get the code at the pinned commit
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/LLM4Chem.git
cd LLM4Chem
git checkout --detach 43ab5fccd14514ddf756534d18a6917e7e11d0ae
steps.explanation: The README says to clone the repository and change into the folder. The detach line pins the commit this page was written from. The README gives no dependency install command, so none is invented here.

quotes.text: Clone this repo to your machine, and `cd` to the folder.

steps.title: Query the model
steps.shell:
python3 - <<'PY'
from generation import LlaSMolGeneration

generator = LlaSMolGeneration('osunlp/LlaSMol-Mistral-7B')
generator.generate('Can you tell me the IUPAC name of <SMILES> C1CCOC1 </SMILES> ?')
PY
steps.explanation: The README's generation example, wrapped in a shell heredoc and run from the repository folder so that the generation module is importable. The adapter is downloaded from Hugging Face on first use.

quotes.text: generator.generate('Can you tell me the IUPAC name of <SMILES> C1CCOC1 </SMILES> ?')

steps.title: Reproduce the authors' evaluation instead
steps.shell:
python generate_on_dataset.py --model_name osunlp/LlaSMol-Mistral-7B --output_dir eval/LlaSMol-Mistral-7B/output
python extract_prediction.py --output_dir eval/LlaSMol-Mistral-7B/output --prediction_dir eval/LlaSMol-Mistral-7B/prediction
python compute_metrics.py --prediction_dir eval/LlaSMol-Mistral-7B/prediction
steps.explanation: The three commands the README gives for evaluating on SMolInstruct: generate, extract the tagged answers, then compute metrics. By default they cover all tasks, and a tasks argument limits them.
steps.source_locator: README: Evaluation on SMolInstruct, steps 1 to 3

outputs: Step two returns the model's reply to the query, with the answer inside a tag such as <IUPAC>.
Step three writes generated responses into the output directory, extracted answers into the prediction directory, and prints the metrics for each task.
limitations: These commands were read from the repository README at commit 43ab5fccd14514ddf756534d18a6917e7e11d0ae and have not been executed by Rewire.
The README gives no dependency installation step and no pinned package versions, so the environment has to be worked out from the code.
The sources give no hardware requirement for inference, only that fine-tuning used four GPUs.

notes: A small molecule chemistry model that a protein benchmark prompted; the page says so rather than presenting it as a protein model. The released repository holds a LoRA adapter only (84,047,501 bytes), so there is no parameter count and no context length to record, and the base model mistralai/Mistral-7B-v0.1 carries its own terms which were not read. The model card links the code at github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/LLM4Chem, while its usage section links github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/LlaSMol, a different address; the README read here came from the LLM4Chem repository, whose own text calls itself the official code repository. No licence for that repository was saved, so the code licence is recorded as not stated. The structured released date is null: the Hugging Face createdAt field is a repository creation date, not a stated release.
